title: The jet that fell 26,000 feet in one minute

beats.text: Thirty-five thousand feet. Then, in about one minute, this jet fell almost the height of Mount Everest.
Nine people were on board. Here's what we know.
Sunday, November 1st. A 22-year-old Learjet 60 takes off from Austin, Texas, heading for the Bahamas.
It climbs to 35,000 feet, above the clouds, over Florida.
But around it, scattered storms are building.
The pilot radios Miami. Light, clear ice... manageable. And moderate turbulence.
beats.label: CLEAR ICE

beats.text: Clear ice is smooth and see-through. It's hard to spot, and it changes the shape of the wing.
The crew asks to climb 2,000 feet higher.
And then... the radio changes.
Mayday. Descending 10,000 feet per minute.
Then... overspeed. 20,000 feet per minute.
Overspeed means faster than the jet's safe limit. The controls get heavy, and the whole frame is under huge stress.
In about one minute, it drops 26,500 feet. Almost the height of Mount Everest.
That's more than twice as fast as a skydiver falls.
Just before one in the afternoon, it hits the ground in Palm Beach County, close to homes and a shopping centre.
Florida's governor said it looked like a missile going down. It left a crater by the road.
No one on the ground was reported hurt. But 600 neighbours had to leave their homes.
So what made this jet fall like a stone? Investigators don't know yet.
The NTSB will look at the weather, the ice, the radar data, and the wreckage.
Nine people lost their lives. The cause is still under investigation.
Follow, and we'll explain what investigators find.
